EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a characteristic pair of strong S=O modes for a sulfonic acid around ~1030 and ~1280 cm⁻¹ (observed 1032 and 1281), plus a band near ~910 cm⁻¹ consistent with an S–OH deformation. The prominent 695 and 662 cm⁻¹ bands fit aryl C–Cl stretching expected for a chloro-substituted ring. Aromatic C–H stretching at 3073 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) and a ring C=C band at 1595 cm⁻¹ further support an aromatic system. Among the candidates, O=S(=O)(O)c1cccnc1Cl uniquely provides both the sulfonic acid group and a chloro substituent to account for this pattern; fluorinated-only candidates lack the S=O pair and multi-chloro phenols do not explain the ~1032/1281 combination.
